content.html:
应@Bunsei大佬的指示，测试一下 R9700采样后端从原生换成 Radiance 加速的生成速度。

结论：同一条 H3 参考图生视频工作流（1344×768 / 294帧 / 20步 / seed 12345 / 6参考图），采样后端从原生换成 Radiance，全流程 4650s → 2314s，加速 2.01×。前置条件：ComfyUI ≥ v0.45.0、原生组件按 gfx1201 编译、实例启动加--reserve-vram 22。双卡 TP 在 X99 + IOMMU 平台不可用（还没测通，后面再研究）。

上对比图片：

环境

项值
硬件X99-TF / E5-2696 v3 / 128G ECC / 双 R9700 32G (gfx1201)
系统Ubuntu 26.04.1 / ROCm 7.2.4 / torch 2.14.1+rocm7.2
ComfyUIv0.44.0 →v0.45.0（Radiance 硬依赖）
插件codeberg.org/Bunsei/ComfyUI-H3-RDNA4v0.2.0，装到custom_nodes/ComfyUI-H3-Video-Radiance
编译python tools/build_native.py --arch gfx1201 --jobs 16，约 5 分钟；check_environment.py返回 ok:true

工作流接入

不改动原生骨架：UNET → 采样器之间插H3 视频加速（H3RadianceAccelerator，INT8 QK＋FP8 PV，devices 0），条件编码换H3 参考素材与提示词（H3RadianceReferences），解码换H3 视频解码（H3RadianceDecode）。Qwen 32B NVFP4-AWQ 编码器直接沿用「高精度加速」线性档。

测试配置（32GB 单卡档）

节点参数值
采样精度INT8 QK＋FP8 PV
激活缓冲位置显存
每卡预留显存4096 MiB
每卡主机权重池24576 MiB
暂存线性权重开
复用主干输入缓冲开
前馈/线性分块4096 / 4096
ComfyUI 启动--reserve-vram 22

实测数据

指标原生Radiance加速比
全流程（同工作流同 seed）4650 s2314 s2.01×
采样每步≈210 s（按总时长扣除预处理/解码推算）101.5 s（20 步全程 101.3~104.7 s，零衰减）≈2.07×
预处理（6 图 1344×768 match + 音频基准）—172 s—
出片1344×768 / 294 帧 / 24fps / 12.25s完全一致—
文件体积12.4 MB12.5 MB—
视频对比https://youtu.be/7dSj4cW1PaEhttps://youtu.be/t-0brZVj774—

画质体检（边缘密度法，抽 1/3/5/7/9/11 秒共 6 帧，单位 %）：

Radiance: 7.48 15.74 7.39 10.67 15.95 15.74
原生: 8.02 15.59 8.30 9.72 13.44 17.09

两版逐秒几乎重合，全部在健康带内，无 latent 崩坏。同 seed 下 INT8 QK＋FP8 PV 与原生精度数值不逐像素一致，构图/动作一致。

坑（现象 / 根因 / 解法）

现象根因解法
_forward_unimplemented() got an unexpected keyword argument 'transformer_options'Radiance 替换diffusion_model._run_blocks，v0.44 的 minimax 前向是手动逐块迭代、无此方法ComfyUI 升级 ≥ v0.45.0（git fetch --tags后git checkout v0.45.0）
worker 启动报VRAM does not cover the fixed costs before a single pool is sized（short by 3.29 GiB，报告显示主进程已占 20.77 GiB）Comfy-Kitchen 量化加载（fast_disk 策略）绕过 torch 分配器，Radiance 的 free_memory / partially_unload 驱逐不动实例启动加--reserve-vram 22，DiT 部分加载，卡净空升至 ~24 GB
预处理只跑 40 秒后报Qwen attention requires CUDA/ROCm tensors on the same device--lowvram把 Qwen 文本编码器整体压到 CPU不要用--lowvram，用--reserve-vram
双卡报GPU 1 is not visible to ComfyUI实例带CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0双卡模式去掉该环境变量
双卡 TP 单步 1037 s 起步、首步 25 分钟未完成（单卡对照 419 s/步）X99 + IOMMU 转译（DMA-FQ）下 P2P 同步代价爆炸，激活缓冲/张量交换走主机的模式每步流量翻倍本平台判死；需 Resizable BAR / 现代 PCIe 平台再测
单卡速度掉到 256~419 s/步激活缓冲挪内存 + 未开暂存/复用缓冲显存激活缓冲 +weight_staging+reuse_hidden_buffer，三项缺一不可

注意点

  • INT8 有效权重容器 ≈ 18 GiB，设计为部分驻留显存 + 锁页权重池 DMA 直读（与计算重叠），权重不常驻显存不是降速路径。
  • worker 启动顺序是先装权重容器和 IPC，再核算激活缓冲 + headroom + 队列空间；不够时报错附精确账本（card total / already held / arena / short by），按账本挤空间：--reserve-vram→ headroom 4096→2048 → IPC 4→2 GiB → 分块 4096→2048。
  • 采样记录在~/.cache/ComfyUI-H3-Video-Radiance/runs/*.json（含 worker_log 与 memory_handoffs），预处理/解码记录分别在preprocessing/、decoding/。
  • --reserve-vram 22会让主进程 DiT 部分加载，跑原生（非 Radiance）工作流前建议去掉该参数重启实例。

以上为单卡 32G 数据。双卡 TP 的平台前提（P2P 直通、Resizable BAR）不具备之前不再浪费时间（双卡 TP 还需要继续研究配置）；有现代平台数据的欢迎贴一下对比。

content.html:
inference-optimisation

An agent skill forhill-climbing the speed of a local LLM serveron any hardware and any quantization. It covers:

  • single-user and concurrent decode
  • speculative decoding
  • prefill
  • KV cache size
  • startup time and time to first token

It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check.

It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow:

  1. Compute the theoretical ceiling.
  2. Change one thing at a time.
  3. Measure against interleaved controls.
  4. Log every result, including the failures.
  5. Gate on long-context retrieval.
  6. Qualify a clean, pinned build before publishing.

It works with Claude Code and any agent that loadsSKILL.md-style skills. Any model can also follow it from [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md).

What we've been able to accomplish

Results from the hill-climbs this skill was distilled from. Every number was measured on the hardware named; see the linked sources for methods and raw data.

| Hardware | Model / quant / engine | Before → after | |---|---|---| |Intel Arc B390 iGPU(laptop, 64 GB unified LPDDR5X, ~115 GB/s) | Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, EXL3 4 bpw, SGLang XPU + MTP | Decode, 1 user: 43.6 →53 tok/s(median)<br>Decode, 4 users: 84.7 →103 tok/s<br>Prefill 32K: 1,037 →1,660 tok/s<br>Prefill 256K: 297 →628 tok/s(2.1×)<br>KV cache: 264K tokens →4 × 256K<br>Startup: 113 →43 s<br>Registry Lab gates: decode 28.6 →41.0, prefill 255 →667| |Intel Arc Pro B70| Qwen3.8-27B, EXL3 4 bpw, vLLM + custom XPU kernels | Decode:91.2 tok/sat 1 user,365at 16 (prose, thinking on)<br>Same card with llama.cpp Q4_K_M: 25.0<br>Prefill 4K/32K/128K/254K: 1,654/1,434/928/650 →2,421/2,259/1,415/911<br>Agent-session replay: 193 →147 s| |Intel Arc Pro B70| Same model, SGLang + the same kernels | Decode, 1 user:82.6 tok/s, vs vLLM 75.7 on the same card and day | |RTX 3090| Qwen3.8-27B EXL3 3 bpw + MTP |96.2 tok/sprose /141.1code, 1 user | |RTX 3090| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B EXL3 3 bpw + MTP |251.7 / 357.9 tok/s, 1 user | |RTX 3090| Flash-Next EXL3, 256K context | MTP: 45.5 →65.6 tok/s| |4× H200 NVL| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, vLLM + speculative decoding | Crashed under load →229.1 tok/sdecode,17,546 tok/sprefill; all six gates pass |

Sources:

  • local-ai-registry:
  • Ornith B390 recipe, with the full hill-climb log inPR #453
  • the RTX 3090 and H200 recipes
  • trellis-serve:
  • xpu/README.md,xpu/docs/PROGRESS.mdandxpu/docs/SGLANG.mdfor B70
  • cuda/README.mdfor the RTX 3090
  • qwen-serve

Reading the B390 result

That run is the one this skill grew out of. Its ceiling calculation said:

  • Decode:100 tok/s for one user was only reachable with two useful speculative drafts. This model's draft head accepts ~14% at depth 2, so the practical target was ~88–97 tok/s. We reached ~55% of it; the rest is GEMV kernel efficiency.
  • Prefill at 256K:we reached 628 tok/s against a ~670–684 tok/s ceiling.

The skill makes the agent compute this up front, so it can tell you early when a target is above the physics.

How it works

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
measure HW ─▶ │ THEORY.md: bytes/token ÷ bandwidth, FLOPs/token ÷ 50% peak, KV │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│
baseline ─▶ profile ─▶ pick lever (ceiling gap × likelihood) ─▶ configs/NEW.json
▲ │
│ queue.sh ctl NEW ctl (serialized, AC-only,
│ memory watchdog, ≥6 samples, medians)
│ │
PLAN.md + ledger.jsonl ◀── accept only if it beats BOTH neighbouring controls ──┘
│ and regresses nothing by >3%
▼
long-context needle gate ─▶ concurrent full-KV soak ─▶ plateau? ─▶ pinned clean build
─▶ acceptance gates ─▶ publish

The skill has three parts:

[SKILL.md](skills/inference-optimisation/SKILL.md): the procedure.

  • Inventory, ceilings, ground rules, the loop and lever order.
  • When to stop, how to qualify and publish, and how to report.

[references/](skills/inference-optimisation/references): loaded only when needed.

content.html: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. We characterize the mechanism a VLM uses to decide where to look before it looks. The mechanism has four main parts. First, binding heads match the relevant text tokens against the image and resolve them into pointers to the matched image region. Second, the same binding heads bind each written answer to the region it came from, and the model turns it into a progress signal: a cursor, the position in the image up to which the list has been written. Third, a select step chooses the nearest unwritten region after the cursor, or stops. Finally, gaze heads execute the chosen pointer and return a concept of what is drawn there, which language heads and the late MLPs turn into a word in the language of the question. We validate each part of this mechanism through causal patching in Qwen3-VL models on a synthetic visual retrieval task, and test our mechanisms against alternative hypotheses. We further show that the mechanism holds across input formats, natural photographs, and languages, and that its binding, relay, and gaze heads appear at every model size from 2B to 32B. This work allows us to investigate how a VLM turns a question and an image into a sequence of answers, layer by layer and token by token. More broadly, it opens a way to study how models plan over complex multi-step tasks with long rollouts. Our project is available at https://plan.baulab.info/

ui: Llama UI design system: tokens, surfaces and fonts (#32468)

  • ui: bring @ggml-org/llama-ui into ui/lib/ui

The design system package (tokens, fonts, surfaces, components and Model UI), so far in the temporary ggml-org/llama-ui repository at edaf518, moves to its home in ui/lib/ui, built with @sveltejs/package and published as @ggml-org/llama-ui from here. ui/lib holds the packages, one folder each. Its references to tools/ui now name ui/apps/chat, its package.json points at this repository, and the UI workflow type-checks and packs it. ui/README.md describes the layout.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

  • ui: Llama UI design system: tokens, surfaces and brand

The design system from allozaur/docs/storybook-overhaul: three tiers of tokens, matte glass surfaces, Llama Sans and Llama Mono, and the base components on the new tokens (Tabs and GlassKey among them). It also restyles the stack's features with it, replacing the plain stand-ins they used until now. DESIGN.md is generated from the tokens. The Storybook that documents it is the next PR.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

  • ui: have Llama Chat use @ggml-org/llama-ui for its base components, tokens and fonts

Llama Chat kept its own copy of the design system: 29 base components, the three tiers of tokens, the surfaces, the theme and the fonts, next to the 12 components ui/lib/ui held. The copy goes, and the library gets what it lacked.

ui/lib/ui

  • the 17 base components the app had and the library did not (alert,

  • the inset-group and selected-row tokens and surfaces
  • sources import each other by relative path instead of $lib, which in an

app points at the app's own src/lib

  • theme.css no longer imports tw-animate-css: it is a peer dependency that

the consumer imports before the theme, as it does Tailwind

  • 0.3.0

ui/apps/chat

  • imports the base components as @ggml-org/llama-ui/ui/<name> and cn/tv as

@ggml-org/llama-ui/utils; app.css imports the library's theme.css

  • compiles the library from source, with no install or build of it:

scripts/vite-plugin-llama-ui.ts resolves its entry points and what it imports, and svelte.config.js gives TypeScript the same paths

  • src/lib/components/ui, styles/tokens, styles/surfaces.css and assets/fonts

are removed; components.json moves to the library

Builds

  • CMake stages ui/lib/ui next to the app, keeping the layout of ui/, and

rebuilds when a library source changes

  • the Dockerfiles copy the library's sources; the Nix derivation takes ui/

as its source

The built CSS has the same rules in the same order, apart from one zero-specificity rule and the @font-face rules moving, plus ten utilities and two tokens that only the library's own components use.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

  • ui: AGENTS.md places Llama UI in ui/lib/ui

Llama Chat's AGENTS.md says where each part lives: Llama UI is ui/lib/ui, and Chat imports its tokens, fonts and base components from there.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

  • ui: Llama Sans and Llama Mono from llama-brand's latest, and shell commands marked in bash code

The fonts in ui/lib/ui come from llama-brand's latest, with optical sizes from 10 to 36. Bash code blocks mark shell commands and flags.

content.html: Cyber-range and capture-the-flag scenario construction remains labor-intensive because authors must coordinate infrastructure, vulnerable services, attack paths, artifacts, and success conditions. LLMs can propose detailed exercises, but plausible descriptions do not guarantee deployable software or verifiable objectives. We present ScenarioForge, which turns high-level requirements into resource-grounded topologies, services, traffic, segmentation, and challenge chains, then instantiates and validates them in the Common Open Research Emulator (CORE). The ScenarioForge Execution Dataset contains 226 materialized scenarios covering 294 Vulhub images and all 85 custom-built challenge-resource generators developed with our AI-assisted scaffolding. All 226 passed construction, preview, sequencing, deployment, strict runtime validation, and live artifact checks; their 867 steps, each an individually verifiable challenge objective, comprise 457 vulnerability-backed and 410 generated-resource-backed instances. In a separate 50-prompt matched benchmark, ScenarioForge+Qwen3.8 and ScenarioForge+GPT5.6 each achieved 50/50 (100%) topology/build success and 160/160 intent fields; direct frontier generation reached 41/50 builds and 147/160 fields only with the full cumulative scaffold: structure, vocabulary, policy, and container-image guidance. The test still omitted ScenarioForge's downstream challenge-resource generation, dependency/flag sequencing, deployment, and live validation. The artifacts support operationally rich, reproducible exercises for training and evaluation.

items.title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent
items.summary: Continual reinforcement learning requires adaptation to changing conditions while preserving performance under previously encountered dynamics. It was investigated whether specialists generated by evolutionary search can provide a reusable memory when combined with environment detection and failure-driven search. The…

content.html: Continual reinforcement learning requires adaptation to changing conditions while preserving performance under previously encountered dynamics. It was investigated whether specialists generated by evolutionary search can provide a reusable memory when combined with environment detection and failure-driven search. The Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent (ENA) evolves small neural networks without gradients, archives selected policies by detected dynamic regime, and retrieves them through Bayesian policy reuse. The architecture was evaluated in non-stationary CartPole and HalfCheetah environments. In the 30-replicate CartPole ablation, the complete architecture achieved a mean success rate of 83.2% across the five test environments. Among variants that learned the harder CartPole environments, the complete architecture showed the most consistent retention. A selection ablation also showed that the retrieval rule affected performance. In the evaluated sequences, ENA adapted more slowly than PPO on CartPole and achieved lower returns than SAC on HalfCheetah. The evidence concerns the complete architecture and does not isolate gradient-free optimization as the cause of retention or establish superiority over other continual-learning methods.

items.summary: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. content.html: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. We fit BSIM4 parameters to measured I-V curves of SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) transistors at 77 K using a neural surrogate of NGSpice. The surrogate maps compact-model parameters and device geometry to the complete set of output and transfer characteristics. Extraction is a bounded least-squares search: a bank of NGSpice simulations supplies initial candidates, finite differences of the surrogate supply the local Jacobian, and NGSpice re-simulates the resulting cards before selection. On 18 measured geometries, we compare a search over seven card parameters with a search over 43 parameters selected by NGSpice sensitivity. Relative to NGSpice re-simulations of the previously released cards, the two searches reduce the in-sample mean relative root-mean-square error (RRMS) by 17% and 26%, respectively. The 43-parameter search has the lower overall error, but the seven-parameter search has the lower mean on high-bias curves, and some individual curves have higher error than with the released cards under both searches.

items.title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
items.summary: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs. A batch-normalized projector removes this component, so regu…

content.html: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs. A batch-normalized projector removes this component, so regularization after the projector cannot correct it, and the differences between representations shrink until they collapse. We propose SADL (Supply And Demand Loss), which keeps the original training objective and constrains the encoder directly when needed. SADL compares the representation differences that the projector output demands with the differences the encoder can retain and pass on to the projector, and adds a constraint on the encoder only when supply falls short of demand. It works with different Demand Regularizers and introduces no auxiliary networks, additional trainable parameters, or architectural changes. In single-task and jointly trained four-task LeWorldModel (LeWM) and INTACT experiments, SADL lowers the collapse rate over ten random seeds from 50% to 0%. After one epoch of training, encoder effective rank is 3.4-6.4 times that of the corresponding baseline without SADL, and latent prediction error falls to 1/20-1/303 of it. Without additional tuning, SADL stays robust as its loss weight spans orders of magnitude, and with several Demand Regularizers INTACT exceeds 95% mean search-free control success. On four image datasets, SADL also consistently improves accuracy and stability across random seeds. These results show that matching the representation differences a regularizer demands with the differences the encoder can supply leads to faster and more stable representation learning in control and image classification.

材料科学智能体MatOS正式开源！大幅提高材料研发任务成功率

思邈2026-11-1714:09:40来源：量子位

筛材料、找配方、开发新模型…拿下多项科研任务

允中 发自 凹非寺

量子位 | 公众号QbitAI

大模型智能体已经能够检索文献、调用模拟软件，甚至与自动化实验室协同工作。但要让它们独立完成一项完整的材料研究，仍然面临挑战：

一项研究可能要从数千万个候选结构中逐级筛选，或在数百个合金配方中反复搜索，持续数天，并根据中间结果不断调整计划；每接入一个新的数据库或软件，往往要重新搭建流程；一项研究中积累的经验，也很难被其他研究复用。

为此，北京中关村学院、中关村人工智能研究院（中关村两院）于今年九月发布年度科研进展——MatOS，一个面向材料研发的科研智能体系统。

该项目由中关村两院AI材料研究所团队构建，将数据、知识、工具、技能、角色和工作流统一组织为科学资产，支持研究者和MatOS自身在已有资产之上构建新能力，通过有状态工作流执行研究任务，并将经过检查与审查的资产修订用于后续研究，使科研能力在使用中持续进化。

目前，MatOS的资产库已包含3,135个数据集、386项技能、104个工作流和51个专家角色，并集成48款材料计算软件；技术报告已在arXiv发布，代码已在GitHub开源。

在3项智能体基准和8个研究案例中，MatOS完成了从端到端自主研究、工具调用到大规模筛选、配方设计和新方法开发的多类任务，例如：

在端到端自主科研基准ResearchClawBench上，与采用相同底座模型的Codex CLI相比，平均得分高33.6%，材料任务高80.8%；

在材料软件使用基准MatTools上，与Codex CLI、Claude Code采用相同的底座模型时，完整问题成功率达到97.96%，为三者最高；

构建层次化筛选流程，从3000多万个候选结构中筛选出97个固态电解质候选；

支持开发合金熔点预测模型DuoCompNet，在固定测试集上的平均绝对误差降至3.18°C，比次优模型低13.6%。

从回答问题到开展研究，再到持续产出高质量科学资产

近年来，ChemCrow、LLaMP等工作让大模型能够调用专业工具，MARS等系统将智能体与自动化实验连接起来，科研智能体正在从回答问题走向开展研究。

材料研究对智能体系统提出了三方面要求：

数据库、模拟软件和机器学习势（用机器学习模型近似原子间作用力、加速模拟的方法）不断出现，要求系统无需重建即可接入新能力；

研究跨越文献分析、计算和实验，要求系统能够在长周期任务中保存状态、检查结果；

模拟时长、采样策略等经验大多来自实践，系统要能存储这些经验，并在后续任务中有效复用。

MatOS以三大设计回应这些要求：分层科学资产图组织并扩展研发能力，有状态自适应工作流调用资产执行任务并保存证据，证据驱动的资产进化将可复用的经验转化为经过检查与审查的资产修订。

MatOS整体架构：分层科学资产图、有状态的自适应工作流和证据驱动的资产进化。

三大设计：构建、执行与进化

分层科学资产图：组合已有能力，构建新能力

MatOS将数据、知识、工具、技能、角色和工作流，组织为六类科学资产。

每项资产都有唯一标识、声明的依赖关系和来源记录，既可以直接保存内容，也可以引用外部数据库或计算软件。

资产之间通过依赖、调用、证据、验证等类型化关系相连，智能体接到任务时，按照这些关系组合所需的能力。

其中，技能相当于一类研究问题的操作规程，规定何时使用、如何选择方法、需要哪些前提、如何执行以及如何检查结果；角色是由职责说明和可调用资产定义的专家智能体；工作流描述多个研究阶段如何衔接。同一技能可以供多个角色使用，同一角色也可以参与不同的工作流。

研究者和MatOS自身都可以在已有资产之上构建新的能力。

研究者可将数据库、软件或方法登记为资产，按接口与依赖关系组合为技能、角色或工作流；MatOS也可依据任务证据新建或修订资产，经检查与审查后供后续任务复用。资产的使用和修订均有记录，每一次改进都可以追溯。

MatOS科学资产的组织方式：（a）六类资产分属四个语义层，从数据、知识、工具、技能逐层抽象到角色和工作流；（b）以电池角色为例，角色从资产图中选取并组合数据、知识、工具、技能和工作流。

有状态自适应工作流：稳定执行与按需调整

工作流资产是可复用的流程描述，一次具体研究则通过执行图运行。执行图中的每个节点都写明目标、输入输出、完成条件和所引用的资产。系统按图调度和检查，只把方法选择、计划调整和异常解释等需要判断的环节交给智能体，需要研究者确认的步骤可以设为人工节点。

由于大模型面对相同输入也可能给出不同输出，长任务中的决策容易随上下文变化而偏离目标，因此MatOS通过显式的步骤和检查条件减少了执行对模型会话的依赖，降低了多步执行中偏离研究目标的风险。

执行图快照、节点状态、结果和事件记录都保存在系统中，独立于模型的会话。

耗时数天的计算交由后台执行，完成、需要输入或失去响应时，系统主动通知智能体；等待外部结果或人工输入的任务会保留进度，之后继续执行。每项输出都关联到产生它的节点和执行尝试。

中间结果可能要求调整后续步骤，例如先补充一步验证，再让后续分析以验证结果为准。这时，智能体或研究者可以提出对执行图的调整，增加或修改节点、改变依赖关系。调整须通过结构、策略和编译三道检查，通过后形成新版本的执行图；未通过时，原执行图继续运行。每次调整的提案、检查结果和采纳决定都有记录，执行图的演化过程可以完整追溯。

执行图的调整首先服务于当前任务。其中具有复用价值的流程改进，会作为证据进入资产进化，经检查与审查后用于修订相应的工作流资产，供后续同类任务调用。

有状态自适应工作流：节点类型、执行图及其动态调整、持久化状态。

证据驱动的资产进化：在使用中持续改进

用户纠正、失败的工具调用、反复出现的操作和工作流结果，都可能提示某项资产需要改进。

MatOS先评估证据是否充分、问题是否成立、经验能否复用，再定位到负责相应功能的资产：方法选择错误可能需要修订知识或技能，工具行为错误需要修复工具，缺少研究步骤则需要修订工作流；必要时也会新建资产，或同步修订多个关联资产。

例如，若反馈表明分子动力学模拟的平衡时间过短，系统可将对应技能中的平衡时长由50ps改为至少200ps，并增加一项检查，确认原子扩散已进入稳定状态。

候选修订须经过结构检查和基于模型的语义审查：结构检查主要判断是否引入新的结构、接口或组合错误；语义审查则判断修订是否回应了原始证据、保留了方法的适用条件，并与关联资产保持一致。

只有通过检查与审查的修订才会被采纳，后续任务的结果又成为下一轮评估的证据。这些经验保存在模型之外的资产中，基础语言模型的参数保持不变；资产也不绑定特定模型，评测中同一套MatOS分别搭配了GPT-5.4和DeepSeek系列模型。

证据驱动的资产进化：证据评估、目标定位、局部修订、结构检查与语义审查、版本采纳。

基准评测结果

ResearchClawBench要求系统依据文献和原始数据开展研究并提交报告。团队选取化学、能源和材料领域的12项任务，与MIRA、ResearchClaw、EvoScientist、Codex CLI等7个采用GPT-5.4的科研智能体进行比较。

采用GPT-5.4时，MatOS平均得分为19.46，较最佳基线MIRA高11.15%，较Codex CLI高33.6%。材料任务表现更突出：较MIRA高18.7%，较Codex CLI高80.8%。换用成本更低的DeepSeek-V4-Flash时，MatOS平均得分为19.20，同样高于全部基线。

ResearchClawBench化学、能源、材料任务的分领域平均得分与总体平均得分。

成本方面，DeepSeek-V4-Flash配置的单任务平均成本约为0.85美元，不到Codex CLI（2.70美元）的三分之一，得分更高；GPT-5.4配置则以约3.78美元的成本取得最高得分。两个MatOS配置共同扩展了本次评测中的成本—得分帕累托前沿（即在多个目标之间，找到一组各有取舍、但没有一个能被其他方案全面超越的最优选择）。

各系统的单任务平均成本与平均得分（成本为对数坐标）。

允中 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号QbitAI
大模型智能体已经能够检索文献、调用模拟软件，甚至与自动化实验室协同工作。但要让它们独立完成一项完整的材料研究，仍然面临挑战：
一项研究可能要从数千万个候选结构中逐级筛选，或在数百个合金配方中反复搜索，持续数天，并根据中间结果不断调整计划；每接入一个新的数据库或软件，往往要重新搭建流程；一项研究中积累的经验，也很难被其他研究复用。
为此， 北京中关村学院、中关村人工智能研究院（中关村两院） 于今年九月发布年度科研进展—— MatOS，一个面向材料研发的科研智能体系统 。
该项目由中关村两院AI材料研究所团队构建，将数据、知识、工具、技能、角色和工作流统一组织为科学资产， 支持研究者和MatOS自身在已有资产之上构建新能力 ，通过有状态工作流执行研究任务，并将经过检查与审查的资产修订用于后续研究，使科研能力在使用中持续进化。
目前，MatOS的资产库已包含3,135个数据集、386项技能、104个工作流和51个专家角色，并集成48款材料计算软件；技术报告已在arXiv发布，代码已在GitHub开源。
在3项智能体基准和8个研究案例中，MatOS完成了从端到端自主研究、工具调用到大规模筛选、配方设计和新方法开发的多类任务，例如：
在端到端自主科研基准ResearchClawBench上，与采用相同底座模型的Codex CLI相比，平均得分高33.6%，材料任务高80.8%；
在材料软件使用基准MatTools上，与Codex CLI、Claude Code采用相同的底座模型时，完整问题成功率达到 97.96% ，为三者最高；
构建层次化筛选流程，从3000多万个候选结构中筛选出 97个 固态电解质候选；
支持开发合金熔点预测模型DuoCompNet，在固定测试集上的平均绝对误差降至 3.18°C ，比次优模型低13.6%。
从回答问题到开展研究，再到持续产出高质量科学资产
近年来，ChemCrow、LLaMP等工作让大模型能够调用专业工具，MARS等系统将智能体与自动化实验连接起来，科研智能体正在从回答问题走向开展研究。
材料研究对智能体系统提出了三方面要求：
数据库、模拟软件和机器学习势（用机器学习模型近似原子间作用力、加速模拟的方法）不断出现，要求系统无需重建即可接入新能力；
研究跨越文献分析、计算和实验，要求系统能够在长周期任务中保存状态、检查结果；
模拟时长、采样策略等经验大多来自实践，系统要能存储这些经验，并在后续任务中有效复用。
MatOS以三大设计回应这些要求： 分层科学资产图组织并扩展研发能力，有状态自适应工作流调用资产执行任务并保存证据，证据驱动的资产进化将可复用的经验转化为经过检查与审查的资产修订 。
MatOS整体架构：分层科学资产图、有状态的自适应工作流和证据驱动的资产进化。
三大设计：构建、执行与进化
分层科学资产图：组合已有能力，构建新能力
MatOS将 数据、知识、工具、技能、角色和工作流 ，组织为六类科学资产。
每项资产都有唯一标识、声明的依赖关系和来源记录，既可以直接保存内容，也可以引用外部数据库或计算软件。
资产之间通过依赖、调用、证据、验证等类型化关系相连，智能体接到任务时，按照这些关系组合所需的能力。
其中，技能相当于一类研究问题的操作规程，规定何时使用、如何选择方法、需要哪些前提、如何执行以及如何检查结果；角色是由职责说明和可调用资产定义的专家智能体；工作流描述多个研究阶段如何衔接。同一技能可以供多个角色使用，同一角色也可以参与不同的工作流。
研究者和MatOS自身都可以在已有资产之上构建新的能力。
研究者可将数据库、软件或方法登记为资产，按接口与依赖关系组合为技能、角色或工作流；MatOS也可依据任务证据新建或修订资产，经检查与审查后供后续任务复用。资产的使用和修订均有记录，每一次改进都可以追溯。
MatOS科学资产的组织方式：（a）六类资产分属四个语义层，从数据、知识、工具、技能逐层抽象到角色和工作流；（b）以电池角色为例，角色从资产图中选取并组合数据、知识、工具、技能和工作流。
有状态自适应工作流：稳定执行与按需调整
工作流资产是可复用的流程描述，一次具体研究则通过执行图运行。执行图中的每个节点都写明目标、输入输出、完成条件和所引用的资产。系统按图调度和检查， 只把方法选择、计划调整和异常解释等需要判断的环节交给智能体 ，需要研究者确认的步骤可以设为人工节点。
由于大模型面对相同输入也可能给出不同输出，长任务中的决策容易随上下文变化而偏离目标，因此MatOS通过 显式的步骤和检查条件减少了执行对模型会话的依赖，降低了多步执行中偏离研究目标的风险 。
执行图快照、节点状态、结果和事件记录都保存在系统中，独立于模型的会话。
耗时数天的计算交由后台执行，完成、需要输入或失去响应时，系统主动通知智能体；等待外部结果或人工输入的任务会保留进度，之后继续执行。每项输出都关联到产生它的节点和执行尝试。
中间结果可能要求调整后续步骤，例如先补充一步验证，再让后续分析以验证结果为准。这时， 智能体或研究者可以提出对执行图的调整 ，增加或修改节点、改变依赖关系。调整须通过结构、策略和编译三道检查，通过后形成新版本的执行图；未通过时，原执行图继续运行。每次调整的提案、检查结果和采纳决定都有记录，执行图的演化过程可以完整追溯。
执行图的调整首先服务于当前任务。其中具有复用价值的流程改进，会作为证据进入资产进化，经检查与审查后用于修订相应的工作流资产，供后续同类任务调用。
有状态自适应工作流：节点类型、执行图及其动态调整、持久化状态。
证据驱动的资产进化：在使用中持续改进
用户纠正、失败的工具调用、反复出现的操作和工作流结果，都可能提示某项资产需要改进。
MatOS先评估证据是否充分、问题是否成立、经验能否复用，再定位到负责相应功能的资产：方法选择错误可能需要修订知识或技能，工具行为错误需要修复工具，缺少研究步骤则需要修订工作流；必要时也会新建资产，或同步修订多个关联资产。
例如，若反馈表明分子动力学模拟的平衡时间过短，系统可将对应技能中的平衡时长由50ps改为至少200ps，并增加一项检查，确认原子扩散已进入稳定状态。
候选修订须经过结构检查和基于模型的语义审查：结构检查主要判断是否引入新的结构、接口或组合错误；语义审查则判断修订是否回应了原始证据、保留了方法的适用条件，并与关联资产保持一致。
只有通过检查与审查的修订才会被采纳 ，后续任务的结果又成为下一轮评估的证据。 这些经验保存在模型之外的资产中，基础语言模型的参数保持不变 ；资产也不绑定特定模型，评测中同一套MatOS分别搭配了GPT-5.4和DeepSeek系列模型。
证据驱动的资产进化：证据评估、目标定位、局部修订、结构检查与语义审查、版本采纳。

ResearchClawBench要求系统依据文献和原始数据开展研究并提交报告。团队选取化学、能源和材料领域的12项任务，与MIRA、ResearchClaw、EvoScientist、Codex CLI等7个采用GPT-5.4的科研智能体进行比较。

Perplexity crossed a $1B annual revenue run rate today, CEO Aravind Srinivastold Semaforat a live event.The Informationreported previously under $250M at the start of the year and over $750M by August, with Computer driving some of the growth. At usualagent labmultiples (egCognition also crossed $1B, withCursor crossing $4.6B), this would roughly mean that Perplexity is now worth $30-50B — if the unit economics hold up. This is a nice bump on the$20B round in September 2025, and qualifies for our “>$10B fundraise” rule for title stories.

Gathering up some recent Perplexity launches for those catching up:

  • Computer.September’sAutomationslet it pick up recurring tasks where it left off. November’sTeammatestake on ongoing jobs. Computer also runs fully locally on supported Macs.

  • Monitor API.Watch a topic or pageand get a webhook when something relevant changes.

  • Frontier Research.The newresearch labhas access to 10,000+ GPUs and plans to publish papers, data, models, and code.

Deepgram is the voice AI infrastructure behind natural conversation—bringing speech-to-text, text-to-speech, voice-focused LLMs, and agents to teams building with voice AI. For any stack and any tools you already love building with, Deepgram slots in as your foundational voice AI technology. So you have control. Qwen4-Max in the wild

content.html:
Datasette Liteis my port of theDatasettePython application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly andPyodide. I've released a complete rewrite of Datasette Lite using service workers, and it's now almost indistinguishable from the real server-side application.

You can now do all of the following, using a carefully crafted URL tolite.datasette.io:

  • Load client-side Datasette to browse any SQLite database, JSON file, CSV file or SQL script
  • Select a released version of Datasette to load from PyPI
  • Load a specific commit, tag, or branch name from the Datasette GitHub repository
  • Pick from over 100 versions of SQLite to use with Datasette
  • Install additional Datasette plugins from PyPI or URLs to wheel files, including JavaScript visualization tools

The ability to load specific Datasette references, plugins, and SQLite versions makes this a fantastic tool for linking to demos of work-in-progress features or bug reproductions, without needing to spin up a full web server to serve that demo.

As an example, consider the following URL:

https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/demo.db&metadata=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

Follow that link and, after a short loading screen, you'll find yourself on a page that looks like this:

That's Datasette running the newdatasette-maplibreplugin, loading up a database of GeoJSON shapes of countries and displaying both a combined map and individual boundary maps in a table.

Let's break down that URL to see what it's doing:

https://lite.datasette.io/
?install=datasette-maplibre
&url=https://.../demo.db
&metadata=https://.../metadata.yml
#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

The?install=datasette-maplibreinstalls that additional plugin from PyPI. You can pass&install=...as many times as you like to load more plugins.

&url=https://.../demo.dbloads that SQLite database from the provided URL. These URLs need to haveopen CORS headers- I host files like this inGists, because they provide an easy way to get open CORS headers on a web-hosted file.

&metadata=https://.../metadata.ymlloadsthis metadata.yml file. The metadata file adds HTML descriptions to various tables, and to the Datasette homepage. Visitthat homepage herefor a guided tour of the other features of that plugin, all defined in the metadata file.

#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continentis a fragment hash that turns into a location within Datasette - here it's loading the/demo/capitals_and_countriesSQL view, then appendinganotherfragment hash to it (%23is a URL-encoded#) which tells the map plugin to zoom to a certain location and to set the color of the shapes on the map based on thecontinentcolumn in the data.

That URL is doing a lot of work! I wrote more about this trick for building URL-addressable software inURL-addressable Pyodide Python environments

items.summary: We study how to learn an autoregressive next-token generator $f\colonΣ^\star\toΣ$ from a class $\mathcal{F}$, given chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations of length $T$ generated by $f$. content.html: We study how to learn an autoregressive next-token generator $f\colonΣ^\star\toΣ$ from a class $\mathcal{F}$, given chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations of length $T$ generated by $f$. We present a simple algorithm based on bagging, which outputs a majority vote of generators that are trained to be CoT-consistent on bootstrap samples of the training data. For binary token sets, it achieves the optimal sample complexity of $O((d_{\mathrm{VC}}+\log(1/δ))/ε)$, independent of the CoT length $T$, where $d_{\mathrm{VC}}$ is the VC dimension of $\mathcal{F}$. For finite token sets $Σ$, the VC dimension is replaced by a multiclass analogue, the Graph dimension $d_{\mathrm{G}}$, and the sample complexity is optimal up to a $\log|Σ|$ factor. The number of generators in the majority-vote ensemble is $O(\log(T/δ))$, and we show that the ensemble can be distilled into a single generator in $\mathcal{F}$ at the expense of $n\log(nT)$ unlabeled prompts.

items.title: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings
items.summary: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection. TRACE learns from benign system-activity graphs by combining message-passing and to…

content.html: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection. TRACE learns from benign system-activity graphs by combining message-passing and topological representations, then assigns anomaly scores in the same projected embedding space optimized by the contrastive objective. This design captures both local interactions and graph-scale structural deviations without using attack labels during representation learning. A labeled validation set containing benign and malicious graphs is used only to calibrate the anomaly threshold. We evaluate TRACE on StreamSpot, GraSec-IoT, and Unicorn Wget against a supervised graph neural network and the benign-only GraphCL baseline. TRACE obtains F1 scores of 0.923, 0.790, and 0.583, respectively. Compared with GraphCL, this is higher on StreamSpot (0.450) and Unicorn Wget (0.203), but lower on GraSec-IoT (0.975). The supervised model leads on StreamSpot and GraSec-IoT, whereas TRACE has the highest F1 on Unicorn Wget. The mixed results show that topology-aware benign-only learning can improve detection in some graph settings but does not provide a uniform advantage.

content.html:
Strata 装进 Mac：M5 Ultra 256GB 跑 104G 大模型，外加内网台式机 3080 Ti 12G联动

同机器，Strata 用源码命令行装一遍、官方 dmg 装一遍，再跟 mlx-serve 同题对比。先放结论：

  • 壳的差别就一句话：dmg 装完就能用，源码路线六步 setup。跑起来是同一个引擎，速度没有差别。
  • 大内存机上，流式惩罚消失：128GB 机器上 prefill 慢 3–4 倍，256GB 机器收窄到 1.6 倍。
  • 跟 mlx-serve 对比：decode 打平、prefill 慢 1.6 倍、质量 5 题全过。没有任何一维赢，换引擎无收益——路径探索到此闭环。

测试环境

项值
机型Mac Studio，M5 Ultra 36 核，256GB 统一内存
模型unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF，UD-Q4_K_XL 档，104GB 四分片
引擎Strata 0.2.15（app）+ engine 0.1.60-macos-arm64-metal
对照mlx-serve，同机常驻，4.7bpw 同家族模型

两条安装路，都走通了

源码路线：clone →setup.sh，依次干七件事（Python 检查、编 Metal 引擎、下模型、对 sha256、pack 打包、MTP 草稿层、起服务）。全脚本可自动化，适合无人值守。注意 pack 产物 85GB，磁盘要留够。

dmg 路线：装 app → 界面选模型自动下载 → 自动 pack、自动拉引擎组件、自动生成实例 api_key。视觉投影和 DFlash2 草稿层都是界面里点选。装完就能用。

装完核验：dmg sha256 对官方 SHA256SUMS 逐字符一致；spctl报 accepted, Notarized Developer ID。

磁盘账：共 183GB（模型 104GB + pack + 草稿层）。

app 版真实负载 4 小时：90 条请求的账

app 起服务后接进 agent 链路当日常大脑跑了 4 小时，引擎日志留下 90 条真实请求——不是跑分脚本，是长会话真实流量：

指标读数
decode中位 117 tok/s，波动带 48–200
投机解码接受率69.2%（77,182 / 111,531 草稿，MTP + DFlash2）
prefill 冷读均值 ~2.8K，峰值 3.4K tok/s
缓存命中67K 长会话滚到下一轮，221ms 吃完（复用 67K，只读增量 437）
最长会话prompt 67.7K token
驻留全加载后还剩 154,918 MiB 空闲显存，80 个专家常驻（R4 hit path ON）

两条值得单说：

  1. 前缀缓存是长会话的胜负手。agent 负载每轮只增几百 token，命中时 prefill 几乎免费——"上下文越堆越慢"在这套组合上不成立。
  2. 69.2% 投机接受率是真实流量攒的，直接解释 decode 波动带上沿为什么能冲到 200。

跟 mlx-serve 同题对拉

同脚本、temperature=0、usage 回读：

指标Strata UD-Q4_K_XLmlx-serve 4.7bpw判词
decode 热身（512 tok ×3）108 / 133 / 133109 / 115 / 145波动带重叠，打平
prefill 42K（破缓存 ×2）3.2–3.5K tok/s5.6K tok/sStrata 慢 1.6×
短请求 TTFT1–2 ms1–2 ms平
质量 5 题（含代码实跑判卷）55平（n=5）

双引擎共存账：mlx-serve 大脑常驻 + Strata 全驻，memory_pressure 49% free，swap 仅 579MB。256GB 扛两套无压力；小内存机器别照抄这条。

局域网那台 3080 Ti：接入、跑况与用法

Mac 之外，家里还有一台 RTX 3080 Ti 12G老台式机，内存四通道64G（16*4）跑 Strata q2_0（n_ctx 65536，推理模型），走反向隧道接进来。定位：它是隔离面，不是提速面——decode 60–75 tok/s 比本机慢，收益是把粗加工（分类、摘要、改写、批量生成）从本机 GPU 挪开，让本机大脑专注主会话。

11-15 全量矩阵实测定稿的用法：

  • 甜点区：业务输入 ≤35K、输出 ≤8K、单发短会话，响应 10–25s。
  • 派活走 API：任务书自带全部材料，一发一收，结果落盘。DSH 界面手动切台式机只限"新窗口 + 新会话 + 单话题短用"，不堆长对话。
  • 严格串行：并发就是排队，队头阻塞实测 36s。长任务在跑时别插短请求指望即时响应。
  • 禁派计数和多步算术——两边模型都不可信，计算交代码执行。
  • 关机即全断，断得干净：连接拒绝 0.2 毫秒返回，不挂死、不重试风暴、本机零波及。没有自愈，恢复靠对侧重新拉隧道——符合"不常驻、纯手动"的设计。

边界

  1. 质量卷 n=5，只能说"无肉眼可见差异"，不是"质量等价"。
  2. 速度读数全部来自单台 256GB M5 Ultra；16–24GB 机器是流式加载的主场，数字不搬。
  3. 90 条请求是 agent 型负载（长会话、高缓存命中），换聊天型短请求画像会不同。
  4. 台式机数据是 11-15 单轮矩阵，n=1 定稿，后续波动未跟踪。

图片出处

  • 主题图与插图：本机双引擎生图（封面与数据板 H3，运行环境 Qwen-Image-2.1）

content.html:
昨天出差贵阳，行程比较紧张，临时远程连家里机器生成了两段。

同一个驱动脚本，2D 和 3D 各一条，1344×768 / 12.00 秒 / 单条直出，不拼接、无二次编码。

2D 动画版：https://youtu.be/94McV1anMCY

3D CGI 版：https://youtu.be/XD2d_HzkBjo

一、这条片子讲了什么

十二秒，五镜：

时间内容
0–3s剑心前脚往石板上搓起一蓬沙石，直接糊进志志雄眼睛，趁他睁不开眼贴上去砍：上挑斜斩 + 反手斩
3–6s志志雄擦亮眼睛暴起反击，四连击（下劈 / 刺 / 火焰横扫 / 再下劈），两人在胸口高度对砍
6–8s剑心抢出全场最快的高中低三连斩，全被架住，反被震退半步，汗珠甩飞——久攻不下
8–10s单手架着刀，另一只手伸进衣襟，掏出一把银色沙漠之鹰，拇指压开保险
10–12s单臂开火，枪口焰照亮半个庭院，志志雄被掀翻、火焰刀脱手，剑心举枪站着，枪口一缕烟

没写"剑气大战"，也没让两人满场跑——全程贴在一刀距离内，靠腰、肩、手臂和刀转。

二、硬件

项值
显卡NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation 48G（单卡）
系统Ubuntu，CUDA
ComfyUI0.39.0，bf16 文本编码
出片方式294 帧一次生成 → 裁到 288 帧 = 12.00 秒，无拼接、无二次编码

三、规格

  • 分辨率1344×768，24fps，288 帧 =12.00 秒
    （H3 是 17k+5 网格，出 294 帧；尾部 5 帧用ImageFromBatch裁掉，音频用TrimAudioDuration同步裁到 12.00s）
  • 参考图六张，2D 与 3D 混用：
    • <Picture 1~3>剑心：2D 动画全身 / 2D 脸部特写 / 3D 手办
  • <Picture 4~6>志志雄：2D 立绘全身 / 3D 手办 / 3D 火场
  • ref_image_size = match
  • 音轨由 H3 原生联合生成（脚步、搓沙、金属碰撞、火焰、枪声），不是后期配的

    • 混用的原因：2D 图的脸最准（脸部特写清晰），3D 手办给的是材质和体块。只喂纯 3D 手办时剑心的脸会被拉成"通用动漫帅哥"，加上 2D 脸特写之后 X 刀疤和眼型就回来了。

    四、工作流

    官方 Ref2VA 路线：

    UNETLoader(Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_int8)
→ LoraLoaderModelOnly(pika_h3_flex_ref2va, 1.0)
→ LoraLoaderModelOnly(H3_Fight_Flow_V1, 0.9)
→ LoraLoaderModelOnly(H3_Combat_V2, 0.9)
→ LoraLoaderModelOnly(Motion_Repair, 0.7)
→ ModelAttentionBackend(comfy kitchen attention)
→ BasicGuider
CLIPLoader(qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot)
VAELoader(video fp16) + VAELoader(audio fp32)
LoadImage × 6 → MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo → LATENT
RandomNoise → KSamplerSelect(lcm) → SigmasFromList(七值) → SamplerCustomAdvanced
→ VAEDecode + VAEDecodeAudio
→ ImageFromBatch(288) + TrimAudioDuration(12.0) → CreateVideo(24fps) → SaveVideo
    项文件
    底模Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v2_int8.safetensors（31.7G 完整版）
    文本编码器qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors
    VAEminimax_h3_video_vae_fp16/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32
    加速 LoRApika_h3_flex_ref2va_comfy_bf16@1.0
    动作 LoRAH3_Fight_Flow_V1@0.9、H3_Combat_V2@0.9、Motion_Repair@0.7

    **工作流 JSON **：
    wf_2D_final.json
    wf_3D_final.json

    五、加速手段

    手段具体
    Pika 六步蒸馏KSamplerSelect(lcm)+SigmasFromList七值1.0, 0.972973, 0.923077, 0.8, 0.571429, 0.333333, 0.0
    SageAttention启动加--use-sage-attention
    Kitchen INT8 注意力ModelAttentionBackend = comfy kitchen attention
    int8 convrot主模型与 32B 文本编码器均 int8 量化
    说明不叠turbo / DMAD / VBVR / lightx2v —— Pika 本身六步蒸馏，叠了会破坏 sigma 调度

    单条 294 帧端到端474 / 491 秒（含 31.7G 模型加载、六张参考图编码、采样、VAE 解码与落盘）。

    六、运行时间

    片开始完成Total
    2D13:20:0813:28:03474.35 s
    3D13:31:4613:39:57490.88 s

content.html: Latent KV cache compression reduces memory footprint by mapping historical keys and values into compact representations. However, generic compressed key states require reconstruction to native dimension before applying RoPE and computing attention scores, adding sequence-scaling overhead to the decode path. We characterize when a latent KV representation can serve directly as the execution state of pretrained RoPE. For RoPE-based transformers, exact static linear execution of the rotary key path requires the latent-to-native map to preserve the pretrained RoPE action through an intertwining relation, restricting exact mixing to coordinates that share the same RoPE frequency. Guided by this characterization, we build GaugeRoPE, a training-free executable latent KV representation. It combines a RoPE-compatible carrier that preserves the rotary action with an approximate position-independent residual key--value (RKV) correction for complementary key and value information, both evaluated without per-token dense historical K/V reconstruction. On Mistral-7B, GaugeRoPE achieves $5.85\times$ KV compression while maintaining quality close to the full-cache baseline. Additional MHA results validate the construction beyond GQA. GaugeRoPE achieves up to $2.48\times$ the decode throughput of the vanilla uncompressed baseline through direct latent execution.

content.html: We introduce Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, an open and efficient small language model further post-trained from Gemma-4-E4B-it and optimized for speed and intelligence per GB of memory used for fast conversational agents. The model carries forward Gemma's strong conversational capabilities and further improves multi-turn tool use, instruction following, and input grounding for fast, local voice/device assistants, interactive personas, and embedded/Edge interfaces. The model combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power voice/device assistants, interactive characters and robotic/IoT interfaces running on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. Experiments on 21 benchmarks show that Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB achieves the highest average accuracy while generating the fewest output tokens in both reasoning and non-reasoning modes, compared with Gemma-4-E4B-it and Qwen3.5-4B. The model is released with a DFlash drafter. With DFlash, Bolt E4B achieves $2.74\times$ the per-user decode speed of inference without speculative decoding at concurrency~1, and $1.21\times$ the generation throughput of Gemma-4-E4B-it with MTP at batch size 1.

Works withPaperless-ngx 2.x and 3.x, OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude),Ollama (fully local), Azure OpenAI and every OpenAI-compatible API (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, LiteLLM, vLLM, LM Studio, Gemini, Together, Perplexity, …).

  • OCR with PaddleOCR– scans, photos and documents with garbled text are read locally (PP-OCRv5 via ONNX Runtime, no extra container, models ~20 MB). Runs automatically *before* the AI analysis – for documents without text, with poor text or always – or on demand. → [OCR](#ocr)

  • Privacy– the usage telemetry of ONNX Runtime (OCR and local embeddings) is switched off.

Automatic processing

Windows 上 Hermes / DeepSeek Harness 无法启动 —— 排障记录

前言：

前些日子一直使用的好好的，更新下了腾讯管家，Hermes / DeepSeek Harness 通通无法启动，本来使用两个工具是可以互相拿来修复，一下全挂了，只能和另一台电脑的hermes通过聊天方式慢慢排查。困扰了两天，真没想到是这个原因。如果有遇到相同问题的兄弟可以借鉴一二。

记录日期：2026-11-17
环境：Windows 10/11 台式机（公司内网），Hermes Agent v0.23.1（git 安装），DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.3
结论：腾讯电脑管家的网络防护驱动拦截了特定进程的 IPv4 回环连接，导致 Pythonsocketpair()死锁，进而使依赖 asyncio 的客户端全部卡在启动阶段。

一、现象

时间表现
最初ping 127.0.0.1返回"一般故障"，4 发 0 收
同期DeepSeek Harness 启动报ETIMEDOUT 127.0.0.1:<随机端口>（8941 / 5907 / 13620 等，每次不同）
同期Hermes 启动卡住无响应，界面出不来或一直转圈
中间执行sfc /scannow后ping 127.0.0.1恢复，但两个客户端仍无法使用

二、排查过程（按阶段）

阶段 1：确认回环 TCP 是否真的修复

ping走的是 ICMP，与 TCP 是两条独立路径，ping 恢复不代表 TCP 恢复。

# TCP 环回测试
$p = Start-Process python -ArgumentList "-m","http.server","8899","--bind","127.0.0.1" -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden
Start-Sleep 2
$r = Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8899
"TCP环回: TcpTestSucceeded=$($r.TcpTestSucceeded)"
Stop-Process $p.Id -Force

结果：TcpTestSucceeded=True（当时 IPv4/IPv6 都通），说明网络栈层面已恢复。

阶段 2：确认客户端进程状态

Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.Name -match 'hermes|dsh|DeepSeek'} | Select Name,Id
Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Where-Object {$_.LocalAddress -match '127.0.0.1|0.0.0.0|::'} |
Select LocalAddress,LocalPort,OwningProcess | Sort LocalPort

发现：进程起来了，但监听端口列表里没有任何端口属于这些进程—— 进程活着却没建立起本地服务。

阶段 3：逐层验证服务端（模型网关）

客户端连的是自建的 HTTPS 网关（经反向隧道转发到家里的推理服务）。逐层验证：

# 1) 公司出口能否连到网关端口
(Test-NetConnection <网关IP> -Port 9443 -WarningAction SilentlyContinue).TcpTestSucceeded
# 2) 网关是否正常应答（不带 key 预期 401）
curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "code=%{http_code} verify=%{ssl_verify_result}`n" https://<网关域名>:9443/v1/models
# 3) 证书是否有效
curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "verify=%{ssl_verify_result}`n" https://<网关域名>:9443/v1/models

结果：

TCP : True
HTTP : 401（0.168s） ← 网关正常，只是没带 key
TLS verify : 0 ← 证书链完整有效

再看网关的访问日志，确认客户端有没有真的发请求过来 ——发现 Hermes 自己发过一条并拿到了 200：

<公司出口IP> - - "GET /v1/models HTTP/1.1" 200 242 "-" "hermes-cli/0.23.1"

=> 网络、证书、API Key 全部正常，问题不在服务端。

阶段 4：读客户端日志，定位卡在哪一步

& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin\hermes.exe" logs errors
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin\hermes.exe" logs --since 30m

关键错误（每 5 分半循环一次，持续一整天）：

CRITICAL hermes_startup_watchdog: Gateway startup did not reach a live event loop
within 300s (elapsed 300s, 0 extension(s)), holds no progress lease and shows no
CPU progress; dumping all thread stacks and exiting with code 75 (OOF-298).

日志最后一行为Plugin discovery complete: 62 found, 58 enabled后再无输出。

"no CPU progress"是关键线索 —— 不是慢，是阻塞在等待（I/O 或网络）。

阶段 5：看线程栈，找到真实卡点

看门狗已把线程栈 dump 到日志目录：

Get-Content "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\logs\gateway-startup-watchdog.log" -Tail 40

栈顶（主线程）：

socket.py line 298 in accept
socket.py line 633 in _fallback_socketpair
asyncio\proactor_events.py in _make_self_pipe
asyncio\windows_events.py in __init__
asyncio\runners.py line 204 in run
hermes_cli\gateway.py 4529 in run_gateway
hermes_cli\main.py in main

卡在 Windows 上 asyncio 创建事件循环的socketpair()。

Windows 没有原生socketpair，CPython 的兜底实现是：
监听127.0.0.1:<随机端口>→ 自己连自己 →accept()。任一步不通，accept()就永久阻塞。

# Hermes 自带的 Python

content.html:
AI has made finding potential vulnerabilities fast and cheap. Fixing them still takes human judgment, and in open source, that work falls to maintainers. Many are already flooded with AI-generated security findings, including duplicates and reports that aren’t vulnerabilities at all. Another raw scan doesn’t help them. Anyone pointing a new model at a project should ask its maintainers first and come with fixes, not just findings.

Maintainers are under intense pressure from this flood of reports. As Christian Grobmeier, a maintainer of Log4j, has put it, theAI defending open source has to be better than the AI attacking it.

AI shouldn’t add to maintainers’ workload. So, with maintainers, GitHub and Microsoft ran a pilot together: could AI help maintainers ship fixes instead of handing them more findings?

GitHub and Microsoft are usingCodename MDASH, Microsoft’s multi-model agentic scanning harness, to find and fix security vulnerabilities in widely used open source software, strengthening the foundation that much of the world’s code is built on.

The process

Our pilot had two goals: send only findings that matter, and never send a maintainer an unverified finding. Here’s how it worked:

  1. Find.Codename MDASH, an AI system from Microsoft Security, scanned each project using Microsoft’sMAI Cyber modeland suggested fixes for what it found.
  2. Filter.AnAI triage agent from the GitHub Security Lab, built on tailored Copilot skills, removed duplicates, checked validity, and focused on high-impact bugs, so maintainers never had to review raw scan results.
  3. Verify.Researchers from Microsoft FORGE Labchecked every remaining finding by hand.
  4. Report privately.Reports reached maintainers through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, with a proof of concept and a suggested fix.
  5. Fix.Maintainers decided what to fix, how to fix it, and when.

Reports and fixes stayed on GitHub, where maintainers already work.

The result: Codename MDASH, using Microsoft’s MAI Cyber model, flagged thousands of possible issues across the six projects. After AI triage and hand review by seven Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers, maintainers received 99 private reports. As of November 15, they had fixed 55, and 14 of those fixes were already in a release.

What we learned

These lessons come from what the six projects fixed and what their maintainers chose to share. Six projects is a small sample, so read them as early lessons.

1. Fixes matter more than findings

Fixing is where maintainers spend their time. So every report arrived already checked, with a suggested fix to review, adapt, and merge. Maintainers started from a well-scoped patch, not a raw finding.

The first fixes shipped about a week after the initial scan. Caddy’s maintainers fixed all 22 of the reports they received in a week or less. Maintainers used the suggested fixes, some as written and some with changes.

items.title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models
items.summary: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. content.html: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. A model reading a 2021 FOMC statement may already know that inflation rose in 2022, so part of its apparent skill can be memory of the outcome, a temporal form of test-set contamination. We measure this memory on FOMC statements and minutes from 2000 to 2026 by comparing modern open models with chronologically consistent models, which are trained only on text from before a fixed date. Asked about past GDP outcomes given only a date, models that cannot know the answer still reach an AUC of up to 0.64 from priors on dates and eras, so chance is the wrong baseline. Against these memory-free models on the same questions, most modern models recall which years had strong growth. Membership-inference scores sort documents by era and document type rather than by whether a model saw them, as exact counts in an open pretraining corpus show. In real-time nowcasts, every lookahead premium we estimate on US GDP is smaller than the forecast comparison can detect at macroeconomic sample sizes, and none on GDP or inflation survives correction for multiple testing. Lookahead audits should therefore measure memory directly against memory-free models on the same items.

items.title: Memory-Efficient Speculative Decoding with Quantized Draft KV Cache
items.summary: Speculative decoding reduces generation cost, but it stores two KV caches: one for the target model and one for the draft model. content.html: Speculative decoding reduces generation cost, but it stores two KV caches: one for the target model and one for the draft model. We reduce this extra memory by quantizing the draft cache. The target cache and verifier remain in BF16, so that compression cannot change the target model's final correction rule. We first study how to divide precision between keys and values. A naive per-token quantizer makes keys appear much more sensitive: splitting a 12-bit budget, K8V4 beats K4V8 in acceptance by 10.87pp. However, with grouped per-channel keys, the gap becomes -0.25pp. A controlled Qwen test confirms that changing only the key quantizer can erase or reverse the preferred bit split. Hence, following KIVI, we propose K4V4 quantization with per-channel keys and per-token values. Across six model pairs, our method reduces draft cache memory by 66.20%, and combined memory across both caches by 23.95%. Mean acceptance drops from 57.93% to 57.14%, only 1.36% relative. Overall, quantized draft caches can make speculative decoding more memory efficient; as a predictive principle for efficient AI design, key and value precision must be co-designed with the quantizer layout.
